name: War Inc: Rising Rope-a-Dope Technique and Trials Guide
title: War Inc: Rising Rope-a-Dope Technique — Formation Switching and Trials
meta_description: Learn the Rope-a-Dope technique in War Inc: Rising Clan Wars. Leave tower, bait PvP formation, return as attacker for morale advantage. Plus formation testing with Trials feature.
author: War Inc Wiki Team

sections.heading: What Is the Rope-a-Dope Technique?
sections.content: The Rope-a-Dope is a tactical maneuver in Clan War where you deliberately leave a tower as an enemy approaches, let them enter the tower with their PvP formation, then immediately return. By leaving and coming back, you become the attacker rather than the defender. This matters because attackers have a significant morale advantage in Clan War — roughly 30% less morale loss compared to defending. The technique was named after the classic boxing strategy of Muhammad Ali, where he would lean on the ropes and let his opponent punch themselves out before counterattacking.

sections.heading: Two Applications of Rope-a-Dope
sections.content: There are two main situations where Rope-a-Dope shines. First, during Crimson Moon, the attacker morale bonus is even more pronounced. You wait for an enemy to approach your tower, step out, let them hit the tower with their PvP formation, then immediately switch to your tower-busting formation and retake it. Their PvP formation takes heavy losses from the tower defenses while losing morale, and your tower build clears them out. Second, in normal PvP fights, you can use Rope-a-Dope defensively at your castle. When an enemy pushes toward your castle with a PvP formation, move out. They hit your castle with PvP (causing heavy morale loss since PvP is weak against structures), then you return and hit them with your PvP formation. It is essentially a hit-and-a-half — they suffer tower damage plus the PvP fight. The effectiveness depends on tower level and the relative strength of the players.

sections.heading: Mind Games and Counter-Play
sections.content: Experienced opponents expect Rope-a-Dope and will counter it by switching to a tower build after their first PvP hit. When you step out expecting a PvP fight and they come back with a tower formation, your PvP build will struggle against their tower-clear lineup. The counter-counter is to stay put and let them hit the tower again with their tower build — now they have wasted energy switching formations, and you are defending against a suboptimal attack. This creates a layered mind game that rewards players who pay attention to opponent behavior. The trick is not always effective, but it gives you a strong tool in the psychological battle of tower defense.

sections.heading: Trials — Free Formation Testing
sections.content: The Trials feature was added to Clan War to let players test their formations for free before committing real morale. Click on any tower, gate, dragon, or spider on the map, hit the hamburger menu, and select Trial. Your troops fight the objective without spending any morale, movement, or energy. This is a game-changer for optimizing your lineups. You can test: how fast you clear level 1 towers versus level 3 towers, whether backstab or dash works better for your dragon setup, how much damage your spider formation actually does, and whether swapping one buffer for a damage dealer improves your total output. The post-fight breakdown shows troop details (damage output, damage taken, control time) for every unit in your formation. You can see exactly who is underperforming and needs to be swapped, and whether your tanks are surviving the full fight.

sections.heading: Formation Switching Strategy
sections.content: Between tower-busting formations (backstab with maximum single-target damage, tanks with shields, and buffers) and PvP formations (flank or split setups for player-versus-player combat), you need to switch constantly in active war. A recommended workflow: have your PvP formation active for defending towers and fighting enemy players, switch to your tower build when it is time to capture objectives, and have your dragon build ready for dragon windows. Using Trials between switches lets you optimize each formation without wasting precious morale. Running the wrong formation into a fight — like a tower build against a skilled PvP player — will cost you heavy morale and put you back at your castle.
